production.note: Calendar build years of the coupe, following the Chiron record. Start: Bugatti (bugatti-veyron-2004, 2 March 2004): "The first vehicles for this exclusive clientele will thus be delivered in the second half of 2005." End: Bugatti (24 June 2011): "The final order for the Bugatti Veyron has been placed by a European customer", completing the 300 coupés (16.4 and Super Sport); OPENERS (openers-veyron): the last car was "scheduled for completion this autumn", ending production of the coupe. US model years could not be sourced: Edmunds (a database) reviews the '2006 Bugatti Veyron 16.4' as all-new and links 2007-2009 (edmunds-veyron-2006), but no source gives the last US model year. The Grand Sport (open) and Super Sport are separate models.

body.note: Two-seat fixed-roof coupé; the open Grand Sport is sold under its own name.

configuration.note: "The 16-cylinder engine with a capacity of 7,993 cm3"; Evo: "8.0-litre, quad-turbocharged W16" (evo-veyron)

drivetrain.note: "All-wheel-drive, turbochargers and substantial weight set it apart from the lightweight, naturally-aspirated duo"

transmission.note: "Sending power to the ground is a Ricardo of England seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, capable of shifting in just 150 milliseconds"; Bugatti: "seven-gear twin-clutch gearbox" (bugatti-veyron-final). Edmunds describes it as a 'sequential-shift manual'; it is a dual-clutch gearbox (DSG). No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Bugatti's rating is metric: 1,001 PS x 0.98632 = 987 hp. Quote (Bugatti newsroom, 24 June 2011): "The 16-cylinder engine with a capacity of 7,993 cm3, its four continuously variable camshafts and four turbochargers is capable of a top speed of 253 mph, developing 1,001 PS (736 kW)." Bugatti's 2004 release (bugatti-veyron-2004): "1001 PS (736 kW)". No separate SAE rating for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS, as in the Chiron record. Evo's spec panel prints "Max power | 987bhp"; Edmunds (a database) prints "1001 hp", the PS figure.

weightLb.note: 1,888 kg x 2.20462 = 4,162 lb. Quote (Evo spec panel, 'Bugatti Veyron 16.4 | Bugatti Super Sport' columns, by Sam Jenkins and Harry Metcalfe): "Weight | 1888kg | 1990kg", the first figure for the Veyron 16.4. Evo does not label it kerb or dry; it is treated as curb (Evo panels normally give kerb weight, and Evo marks dry figures as dry). OPENERS (openers-veyron, by Tai Matsuo) prints the same "1,888 kg". No Bugatti curb weight was found on the opened Bugatti releases. Single configuration. Under the guide's weight order this is step 2 (a major magazine's specification panel).
